title: $160K Down in ONE DAY! Why I'm BUYING These 15 Stocks
creator: Joseph Hogue, CFA
summary: Joseph Hogue reviews his main E*Trade portfolio after Friday's AI sell-off left his top 15 holdings down $160,000 in a day, partly hedged with call options. He is holding his two Ethereum trusts (ETHA and the Grayscale mini ETH trust), arguing SEC moves toward tokenised stocks make Ethereum the backbone of tokenised finance, with a $4,000-$5,000 target by the end of next year. He is closing out Super Micro Computer (SMCI) via $35-$40 January covered calls and an exit on a $40-$45 rebound, despite still seeing valuation upside. He plans to roughly double his 1,500-share Alibaba (BABA) position at $109 before early-November earnings, betting its Qwen open-source model wins as token volumes explode, and he is still holding Symbotic (SYM). In cybersecurity — his favourite long-term theme — he is picking up more Zscaler (ZS), pauses on Fortinet (FTNT) and Okta (OKTA), and holds CrowdStrike (CRWD) and Palo Alto (PANW). He also endorses SoFi (SOFI) back in at $15.89, holds SoundHound (SOUN) and Grab (GRAB), and trails a Wednesday video on rotating from AI hardware into application names such as SoundHound, Cloudflare, ServiceNow, Snowflake and Salesforce. Calls: ETHA HOLD, SMCI SELL, BABA BUY, SYM HOLD, CRWD HOLD, PANW HOLD, FTNT HOLD, OKTA HOLD, ZS BUY, SOFI BUY, SOUN HOLD, GRAB HOLD, NOW UNCERTAIN. Captions garble several items — Alibaba's model as 'Qin', Mastercard's payments network as 'global patent payments network', and Ethereum price history — tickers and stances above are the companies actually discussed.

calls.thesis: Holding onto his two Ethereum trusts (ETHA plus the Grayscale mini ETH trust, about $1.7m combined, still up ~$300k despite -$28k on Friday); investing in Ethereum as the backbone for tokenised real-world assets after the SEC cleared a path for tokenised stocks, and expects Ethereum back to $4,000-$5,000 by the end of next year.

Tired of the volatility and management/accounting problems; still up ~$93k plus covered-call income.

Still holding on: believes Symbotic changes warehousing/logistics via its Walmart partnership (warehouse robotics/delivery systems) and a SoftBank partnership internationally, despite the fall from its peak.
